title: The graduated Commander-in-Chief powers
ask: Name the three Commander-in-Chief powers, from least to most intrusive, with the ground for each.
items: Calling out the armed forces: whenever necessary, to prevent or suppress lawless violence, invasion or rebellion
Suspending the privilege of the writ: actual invasion or rebellion, when public safety requires it
Martial law: actual invasion or rebellion, when public safety requires it
src: Art. VII, Sec. 18; Sanlakas; David; Lagman (2017)

title: The Sec. 18 safeguards on martial law and the writ
ask: List the safeguards the 1987 Constitution put on martial law and the suspension of the writ.
items: Only for actual invasion or rebellion, when public safety requires it (“imminent danger” deleted)
At most 60 days
Report to Congress within 48 hours
Congress, voting jointly by a majority of all its Members, may revoke; the President cannot set it aside
Extension only on the President’s initiative, if the invasion or rebellion persists and public safety requires it
Congress convenes within 24 hours if not in session, without need of a call
Any citizen may ask the Supreme Court to review the factual basis; decision within 30 days
Martial law does not suspend the Constitution or supplant the civil courts or legislatures
No military jurisdiction over civilians where civil courts function; the writ is not automatically suspended
The suspension applies only to persons judicially charged with rebellion or offenses connected with invasion, who must be charged within 3 days or released
hook: Actual, 60, 48, revoke, extend, 24, citizen-30, Constitution stays, no soldier-judges, 3 days.

title: Why the Court defers on calling out (IBP v. Zamora)
ask: Give the reasons IBP v. Zamora gives for deferring to the President’s decision to call out the armed forces.
items: The only criterion is that calling out “becomes necessary,” a matter the Constitution leaves to the President
There are no textual standards for the Court to apply
The evidence may not be technical proof, and much of it may be classified
The President has a vast intelligence network and must act swiftly
So review is only for grave abuse, and the petitioner must show the judgment was totally without factual basis
src: IBP v. Zamora (2000); Ampatuan v. Puno (2011)
hook: Necessary, no standards, no proof, intelligence, grave abuse.

title: Judicial review of martial law and the writ: the line of cases
ask: Trace the Court’s position on reviewing the suspension of the writ and martial law, in order.
items: Montenegro v. Castañeda (1952): the President’s decision is final, not reviewable
Lansang v. Garcia (1971): reviewable for arbitrariness
Garcia-Padilla v. Enrile (1983): back to Montenegro
1987 Constitution, Art. VII, Sec. 18: any citizen may sue; sufficiency of the factual basis; 30 days
Fortun (2012): the Court waits for Congress (joint and sequential)
Lagman v. Medialdea (2017): sui generis review, independent of Congress; Fortun set aside
src: Gatmaytan, Martial Law Cases lecture; Lagman (2017)
hook: Final, arbitrary, final again, citizen-30, wait, independent.

title: The rules of review in Lagman v. Medialdea (2017)
ask: State the rules Lagman v. Medialdea (2017) laid down for reviewing martial law.
items: The “appropriate proceeding” is sui generis, not certiorari; any citizen may file
The Court’s review is independent of Congress’s
The question is sufficiency of the factual basis, not accuracy
Actual rebellion (Art. 134, RPC) or invasion, and public safety, must concur
The President needs only probable cause
Only facts known to the President at the time count (the Proclamation and the Report), in their totality
Some false facts do not void it if the rest suffice
The Court does not calibrate the choice of power or the area covered
hook: Sui generis, independent, sufficient, actual-and-safe, probable cause, then-known, falsity tolerated, no calibration.

title: Limits on extending martial law (Lagman v. Pimentel III)
ask: Give the only limits on Congress’s power to extend martial law or the suspension of the writ.
items: Upon the initiative of the President
The invasion or rebellion persists and public safety requires it
Congress votes jointly, by a majority of all its Members (“in the same manner”)
Subject to the Supreme Court’s review of the factual basis
No limit on the number of extensions or their length: “a period to be determined by the Congress”
src: Lagman v. Pimentel III (2018); Lagman v. Medialdea (2019)
hook: Asked, persisting, joint majority, reviewable, unlimited.

title: What Olaguer held
ask: State the holdings of Olaguer v. Military Commission No. 34.
items: Military commissions cannot try civilians, even during martial law, while civil courts are open and functioning
Due process means trial by judicial process; military commissions are not courts
Their judgments against civilians are void for lack of jurisdiction
Aquino, Jr. v. Military Commission No. 2 is abandoned
Even with jurisdiction, a tribunal that denies constitutional rights is ousted of it
Lifting martial law ended their authority over civilians; double jeopardy does not bar a civil trial

title: Habeas corpus after a final conviction (In re De Villa)
ask: When does habeas corpus lie against a final judgment of conviction?
items: A constitutional right was denied, resulting in the restraint
The court had no jurisdiction to impose the sentence
The penalty was excessive, as to the excess
hook: Right denied, no jurisdiction, too much.

title: What David v. Macapagal-Arroyo held on PP 1017
ask: Give the Court’s rulings on PP 1017 and General Order No. 5.
items: Valid as a call on the AFP to prevent or suppress lawless violence; not martial law
Void insofar as it ordered the AFP to enforce decrees and laws unrelated to lawless violence
The President may declare a state of national emergency alone
But taking over private businesses (Art. XII, Sec. 17) needs a law from Congress
G.O. No. 5 valid, except its undefined “acts of terrorism”
The warrantless arrests, the dispersals and the Daily Tribune raid were unconstitutional
Decided though moot, under the four exceptions
hook: Call yes, decrees no, declare yes, take over only by law.

title: RA 12287: the State of Imminent Disaster
ask: Give the main features of the Declaration of State of Imminent Disaster Act (RA 12287, 2025).
items: Declared by the President on the NDRRMC’s recommendation (local chief executives in their areas)
Based on a pre-disaster risk assessment of a forecasted hazard with severe projected impacts
A lead time of three days, extendible to five, for anticipatory action
Allows pre-emptive evacuation, prepositioning of teams and goods, social amelioration and release of funds
Lifted when the projected impacts are no longer expected, and automatically when the hazard occurs
hook: Recommend, assess, three days, act early, lift.

title: The foreign-loan power
ask: State the rules on contracting and guaranteeing foreign loans.
items: The President contracts or guarantees foreign loans on behalf of the Republic (Art. VII, Sec. 20)
With the prior concurrence of the Monetary Board
Prior concurrence works in stages: Approval-in-Principle, then signing, then Final Approval before drawdown (Colmenares)
Subject to limitations provided by law (RA 4860; RA 245)
Bond conversions and buybacks are within the power (Constantino)
The Finance Secretary may act as alter ego (Constantino)
The Monetary Board reports its decisions to Congress every quarter
Information on foreign loans must be made available to the public (Art. XII, Sec. 21)

title: What Nicolas v. Romulo held
ask: State the holdings of Nicolas v. Romulo.
items: The VFA complies with Art. XVIII, Sec. 25: the Senate concurred and the US recognized it as a treaty
Whether the US Senate ratified it is a matter of US domestic law
US troops are also here under the Mutual Defense Treaty, ratified by both Senates
Medellin v. Texas does not affect the VFA
US custody of an accused during trial violates neither equal protection nor the Court’s rule-making power
After conviction, detention must be by Philippine authorities: the Romulo-Kenney Agreements were not in accord with the VFA
hook: Concurred, recognized, MDT, Medellin no, custody yes, detention ours.

title: Presidential immunity from suit
ask: State the rules on the President’s immunity from suit.
items: The incumbent President cannot be sued during tenure, though the Constitution is silent (De Lima)
It covers any suit and any act, official or personal, even habeas data (De Lima)
The Court applies it even if the President does not invoke it (De Lima)
It belongs to the President alone: an accused cannot invoke it (Soliven)
The President may waive it and file suit (Soliven)
It does not cover the President’s subordinates (Gloria)
It ends with the tenure: a former President may be prosecuted (Estrada v. Arroyo)
The remedy against a sitting President is impeachment
hook: Sitting, total, automatic, personal, waivable, not for officials, ends, impeach.

title: What Marcos, Jr. v. Robredo held
ask: State the holdings of Marcos, Jr. v. Robredo (PET, 2021).
items: A protest must specify each irregularity and its precinct; bare allegations are not enough
Under PET Rule 65, the protestant picks at most three pilot provinces
No reasonable recovery in the pilots: the protest is dismissed without more
That dismissal also bars the cause of action to annul elections
Annulment would need the Abayon requisites anyway
The PET may annul election results, but only the COMELEC may call special elections
RA 1793’s 20-month period no longer binds the PET
hook: Specific, three pilots, recovery or out, Abayon, annul yes, special election no.
